summary: David dwelling in house of cedar, ark in tent curtains, says to Nathan I dwell in cedar house, ark in curtains, shall I build house for Yahweh? Nathan says do all in heart Yahweh with you. That night word of Yahweh to Nathan: Did I ever ask for house of cedar? I took you from pasture from following sheep to be prince over my people, made great name, gave place, will make rest. Yahweh will make you a house: your seed after you... I will be his father, he my son, if iniquity chasten with rod, but my lovingkindness not depart as from Saul, your house and kingdom established forever before me, your throne forever. David goes in, sits before Yahweh, prays Who am I, what is my house, you have spoken of servant's house for great while to come, is this manner of man? You established Israel forever, now let house be blessed.
whyItMatters: Davidic covenant — promise house, kingdom, throne forever. Often described as unconditional — though the discipline clause in 7:14 and later covenant warnings keep a scholarly debate alive about how unconditional it truly is. Basis for messianic hope: son of David whose throne forever.

themes: you want to build me house? I will build you house

questions.question: What is wordplay house — David wants to build house for God, God says I will build you house?
questions.answer: House (bayit) can mean building (temple) and dynasty (house of David). David says I live in cedar house, ark in curtains, I will build house for Yahweh. God says did I ever ask for house of cedar? You want to build me a house (temple), but I will build you a house (dynasty). Then your seed will build house for my name (Solomon's temple). Pun reverses initiative — God is builder, David beneficiary.

questions.question: What does 'I will be his father, he my son' mean? Does it mean divine?
questions.answer: Adoption formula for kings in ancient Near East — king adopted as son of deity on enthronement day. Not necessarily divine nature in Old Testament sense, but intimate relationship. Hebrews uses for Jesus as greater Son. Promise includes discipline with rod of men if iniquity, but lovingkindness (hesed) not depart as from Saul — unconditional loyalty despite failure, unlike Saul's rejection.

questions.question: Why does David pray 'Who am I, what is my house, you speak of great while to come, is this manner of man?'
questions.answer: David sits before Yahweh (unusual posture — before ark) and expresses wonder — who am I that you brought me from pasture sheep to prince, and speak of future far off (great while to come)? Is this manner of man — i.e., do you treat humans like this ordinarily? Acknowledges grace and future orientation — promise extends beyond his lifetime, to house forever. Model of humility after exaltation.

questions.question: How does this covenant relate to Mosaic covenant? Conditional vs unconditional?
questions.answer: Mosaic (Sinai) conditional: if you obey you will be my people. Davidic unconditional: your throne forever (v16), my hesed not depart. Yet includes discipline (rod). Both held together — unconditional promise provides security, but disobedience brings discipline. After exile, when throne seems fallen, this promise fuels hope for future Davidic king — messianic expectation. A note of honesty: the promise is often called unconditional, but 7:14's discipline clause and the later exile keep the question genuinely debated.

glossary.def: Can mean temple building and dynasty — pun central.
Offspring — singular and collective, can mean Solomon and ultimately Messiah.
Long time, everlasting, indefinite future — throne forever.
